Local Ordinance 99-9 Loitering or Prowling

BE IT ORDAINED BY THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF PINE MOUNTAIN, GEORGIA, AND IT IS HEREBY ORDAINED BY AUTHORITY OF SAME, AS FOLLOWS:

A person commits the offense of loitering or prowling when he is in a place at a time or ina manner not usual for law abiding individuals under circumstances that warrant a justifiable and reasonable alarm or immediate concern for the safety of persons or property in the vicinity.

Among the circumstances which may be considered in determining whether alarm is warranted is the fact that the person takes flight upon the appearance of a law enforcement officer, refuses to identify himself, or makes endeavors to conceal himself or any object. Unless flight by the person or other circumstances make it impracticable, a law enforcement officer shall, prior to arrest for an offense under this code section, afford the person an opportunity to dispel any alarm or immediate concern which would otherwise be warranted by requesting the person to identify himself and explain his presence and conduct. No person shall be convicted of this offense if the law enforcement officer failed to comply with the foregoing procedure or it appears at trial the explanation given by the person was true and would have dispelled any concern or alarm.

Any person violating any of the provisions of this ordinance shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof shall be fined not more than $1,000.00 and/or more than six months in jail.

Rate Schedule:

First Offense $300.00 and 8 hours community service Second Offense $750.00 and 16 hours community service
